description: Minimal: def main(), do: dbg(<<"x", digit(1)>>); @spec digit(integer) :: integer; defp digit(n), do: 48 + n. Interp and JIT both abort in runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs fz_bs_write_field_ref with "integer bit field expects Int"; the .99 AOT fixture shows the same failure. Controls: <<digit(1)>> and <<digit(1), digit(2)>> both succeed, so a direct call is valid until a preceding binary-literal segment shifts the dynamic field carrier. Expected output is "x1". This is distinct from fz-5xp.66, whose closure call fails even as the first field and whose ticket explicitly records direct calls as working. Add a three-door behavioral fixture and repair the construction field/value alignment rather than accepting a runtime tag panic.
title: A binary-literal bitstring segment shifts a following call result into the wrong carrier
